inference.why_the_rounds_moved: A reading the claim left standing was measured and came back for itself, so the model gained a part it did not have. That is a revision and it is counted as one, unlike a round where a competing reading merely falls.
inference.why_the_rounds_did_not_move: The ceiling counts revisions of the model. Nothing about the model moved on either of the two occasions this file has said so. A standing alternative was measured and came back neither confirmed nor refuted, and then the two readings it came back on were found not to be readings of the stage at all and taken off it. Recording what a run found is not a revision, and nor is withdrawing it.
inference.why_parked: Four rounds. What it found is kept: the byte is a gain in front of a curve, a fixed filter stands in front of that curve, and near zero the curve is not smooth -- its order series stops falling where a smooth feature's would not. What it gave up is whether the curve has a state in it, and that was already recorded as something this rig cannot ask: a stimulus with no harmonics of its own cannot be presented from outside, cannot be found among the unit's own voices, and cannot be driven out from under the contamination, each closed by a measurement rather than by an estimate. So nothing here is waiting on a run.

claim:
The byte a page prints `Drive` against sets how hard a signal is driven into a fixed nonlinearity. It does not choose between curves and it does not change the curve: over the settings the comparison can reach, feeding the stage a louder signal at one drive returns the same reading as raising the drive at one input, the reading being the level at each whole multiple of the carrier under the level at the carrier. That is a statement about the stage and not about the signal. If the stage is one curve behind one gain then scaling what it is fed has the same effect whatever it is fed, so all this needs is that both sides of every comparison were made on the same signal, which they were. It is worth saying what it therefore does not need, because the signal is not what the run took it for: the voice is two oscillators about twelve cents apart at nearly the same size, so it beats, and the stage was driven at a level that moved through each take rather than one that stood still. The correspondence survives that untouched. What is read at each multiple of the carrier does not, and nothing here is a harmonic series. The input each setting wants is what that setting's own value gives when it is read as a gain -- twenty times the log of it over 48, in decibels, and 48 is where the page rests the byte rather than an origin chosen here. From setting 8 to 48 the wanted input tracks that law to between a tenth and four tenths of a decibel, against bars of a tenth to four and four tenths that the ladder measures for itself by putting each of its own rungs back from the others. The tightest of those rows is setting 32, where the law is asked to a tenth of a decibel and answers to a tenth. Two bounds, both measured. The byte's bottom three settings return one state -- 0, 2 and 4 agree order for order inside the run's own repeats -- so whatever the byte is there it is not a gain, which would have to be three different ones. Above 48 every setting wants more input than the part can give, and the comparison says nothing about them rather than pinning them to the ladder's last rung. The other standalone drive type is a different curve and not the same one rested somewhere else. No state this type can be put in comes within seven and nine tenths of a decibel of any state of that one, against repeats that agree to two hundredths. What the stage is fed is not the carrier: a fixed filter stands in front of it, and what reaches the curve is a shaped version. The stage's small-signal gain at the carrier is 11.87 decibels at 110 hertz, 20.37 at 220 and 23.08 at 330 -- a tilt of 11.21 decibels, 8.50 of it in the first octave. The level the three were fed is one level: across all 10 rungs of the ladder the three carriers differ in what went into the stage by at most 0.10 of a decibel, which is the worst of the rungs and not a chosen one. And where the ladder stops moving the output, the carrier comes to rest at -39.84, -39.93 and -40.49 decibels -- a spread of 0.65, against a tilt of 11.21 going in. A filter after the curve would carry that tilt onto the ceiling, because a curve that limits puts out what it puts out and anything after it multiplies that; a filter in front changes only how much arrives, so three carriers rest at one level however differently they got there. The ceiling is flat and the gain is not, so the tilt is in front. None of this moves the law above. Feeding one carrier a louder signal at one drive still matches raising the drive at one input, because the filter is the same filter on both sides of every comparison and every comparison was made on one carrier. What it does move is what the curve is taken to be fed: the input a setting wants is the input at the part, and the input at the curve is that input through a filter nobody here has identified. Its shape is not read off these three points -- eight and a half decibels in the first octave is steeper than any one-pole can be, and that is the whole of what the spacing supports. The tilt is a floor rather than a figure, and errs the safe way: the gain at the lowest carrier is the same at the bottom three rungs and is therefore the small-signal one, while at the highest carrier the gain is already falling by the second rung, so the number read there is under that carrier's own small-signal gain and the distance between them is under the true distance.

**The curve does not run out of orders, and near zero it is not smooth.** The byte was swept again on the voice measured to be one component at this note, read to 32 orders, and the series was asked how it behaves high up. At the setting the page rests the type at, the odd orders fall 6.3 decibels an order from the 11th to the 23rd and then stop falling: from the 25th to the 31st they sit at -77 decibels under the first, where the rate the low orders set would have carried them to -109. What is there stands 31 decibels over that, 37 over the same order of the take routed past the effect, and 72 over the floor between the orders in its own take -- so it is neither the voice, nor the chain, nor a floor the reading is sitting on. Across those last four odd orders the series falls 2.6 decibels, which is a power of the order and not an exponential: a curve smooth on the scale of the signal loses its orders faster than any power, and that is the whole of what the two readings differed by. Which power is not settled here. A jump gives 1.9 decibels across these four orders and a kink in the slope gives 3.7, and the repeats of one setting in this record fail to agree by more than the difference between them. A step and a corner are both what the smooth reading was not, and telling them apart is a finer question than the one that was asked.

**Read at one setting of the byte and not across it.** What stands over a high order is what this same stage makes of the voice's other partials, which is bounded by driving a stand-in curve as hard as the unit is driven. Below the resting place the stand-in cannot be brought near the unit's low orders at all -- 11 decibels away at the worst -- so the bound it returns is a number about the stand-in. Above it the low orders match and the drive that matches them is hard enough that the stand-in's own high orders stand over everything the unit shows, which is a bound that admits nothing rather than a reading that failed. One setting is what this run reads, and it is the one the page rests the type at.
named: a linear pre-gain into a fixed curve. Nothing is named about the curve. It is not called memoryless, because every figure was read on one held tone at one frequency and that cannot tell a static curve from one with a state in it; and nothing is said about where it departs from linearity, because the signal it was read on is two beating oscillators and the shape of a curve cannot be taken off that. A name is the first part of a claim to be retracted, and one half of this one already was

The ladder every drive setting is matched against. Its control takes carry the setting each was made at, and their level is the only measurement of what the stage was being given -- nothing inside the type reads its own input.

The control the whole comparison rests on, taken at the drive the ladder was made at. The output moves twenty-six decibels and the orders under the first do not, so two settings that came back at different loudnesses are not being compared through a gain.

The other standalone drive type, asked at every setting of the same byte so that the two can be compared at the value each reaches rather than at the value each rests at.

The 110 hertz carrier. document_rows.why: What the law is written from. The middle number of a printed range is the value the unit powers the byte up holding, so 48 is the byte's own resting place and not an origin picked to make a fit work -- and the other type resting 28 settings further up is what made asking both at every value rather than at their own defaults worth the device time.

era_priors.claim: A nonlinearity on a fixed-point part of this period is a short table or a few multiplies, and it is written once. What a control over it can afford to be is a multiply on the way in; what it cannot afford is a curve per setting, which would be a hundred and twenty-eight tables.
era_priors.why: It says why a gain in front of one fixed curve is the arrangement to look for first. It carries nothing about which curve, where its bend is, or what the byte does at the two ends where the measurement says it is not a gain.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The byte had returned a family of shapes no single input level reproduces, which is exactly what the comparison was built to detect and what it reports for the bottom three settings.

adds: The records say what orders came back at each setting of the drive byte, at each setting of the output level byte, and at each setting of the part's own volume. What is read out of them here is that two of those three are the same control twice -- which is a comparison between two records and is in neither of them -- and that the correspondence between them is the byte's own value in decibels. The bound at the bottom is a comparison within one record that the record does not make, and the reading of the curve's shape is a statement about where a nonlinearity bends, which no band or order figure states.

alternatives.reading: The byte is a selector rather than a gain: each setting loads a curve of its own, and the fourteen curves are not one curve driven fourteen ways.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Every setting from 8 to 48 is reproduced by an input level on a ladder made with the byte held at one value throughout, to inside the bar the ladder measures for itself. A set of independently loaded curves has no reason to be reachable from one of them by changing nothing but the level in front of it, and no reason for the level it takes to be the setting's own value in decibels against the byte's printed rest.

alternatives.reading: What the byte changes is the level after the stage, and the apparent change in distortion is something further down the chain behaving differently at different loudnesses.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The output level byte of the same type was swept at two drives. It moves the output twenty-six and a half decibels and moves the orders under the first by six hundredths of one, at both drives. Nothing after the stage changes what these figures hold, so the drive byte's effect on them is not a loudness effect wearing its name.

alternatives.reading: The part's own volume does not reach the stage's input -- it changes the voice, and the ladder is a ladder of different stimuli rather than of one stimulus at different levels.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The same run took a take routed past the effect at every setting of the volume. Across thirty-six decibels of it the voice's own orders move by eleven hundredths of a decibel at the widest and by one or two hundredths almost everywhere, against repeats that agree to one. The voice is the same voice at every rung and only its level changed.

alternatives.reading: A fixed filter sits in front of the curve as well, so what the stage is fed is a shaped version of the carrier rather than the carrier.

separated_by.observable: The equivalent drive the stage reports at two carrier frequencies an octave apart, each fed at the level that puts the same first order into it.

predicts.no filter in front: The same equivalent drive at both carriers, because a curve fed a sinusoid cares about its size and not its rate.
predicts.a filter in front: Two different equivalent drives, apart by whatever the filter does across that octave.

separated_by.divergence: One decibel across an octave, as the smallest tilt this archive would call a filter: the two shelving bytes on this same type move twelve decibels and the cabinet responses after it move ten point seven through the bottom octave, so a filter flat to a decibel over one octave is not one of those.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: 0.065 dB of equivalent drive. The ladder moves the second order 0.34 dB over the 2.20 dB of input between its two rungs either side of the reference -- 6.47 dB of input per decibel of order -- and the repeats agree to 0.01 dB.

run.stimulus: a note held through the effect on a voice measured to be one component at this same note -- program 79, from a survey of nine of the unit's own voices. Read through the filter these figures are read through, its own orders stand 41.7 decibels under its first at the worst of the first eight, and from the fourteenth order upward it stands at the chain's own floor, 101 decibels under and lower. Not a signal presented at the analogue input: that input reaches this unit's output flat and bypasses every one of its effects, which is measured, sounded at two notes an octave apart and at the levels that put the same first order into the stage

alternatives.taken_up_by: The stage's small-signal gain at the carrier is 11.87 decibels at 110 hertz, 20.37 at 220 and 23.08 at 330 -- a tilt of 11.21 decibels, 8.50 of it in the first octave. The level the three were fed is one level: across all 10 rungs of the ladder the three carriers differ in what went into the stage by at most 0.10 of a decibel, which is the worst of the rungs and not a chosen one. And where the ladder stops moving the output, the carrier comes to rest at -39.84, -39.93 and -40.49 decibels -- a spread of 0.65, against a tilt of 11.21 going in. The run the claim booked against this asked for two carriers an octave apart at matched first order. Three were taken instead of two and they were matched at the part rather than at the stage's first order, which is the stronger form of the same comparison: matching what goes in needs no reading of what came out, and the records show the three carriers were fed one level to a tenth of a decibel without anything being tuned to make them. What the alternative asked to see was a tilt of one decibel across an octave. The first octave alone carries 8.50.

alternatives.reading: The curve has memory. It is not a static transfer function but something with a state in it, and every figure here was read on one held tone at one frequency, which cannot tell the two apart.

separated_by.observable: Whether anything comes back that a curve with no state in it could not have put there. Both readings that would show it -- content away from the whole multiples, and the orders' angles moving as the drive rises -- need a stimulus that carries no harmonics of its own, and say nothing about the stage on one that does.

predicts.a static curve: Nothing off the multiples. Fed one sinusoid a memoryless curve returns energy at whole multiples of it and nowhere else.
predicts.a curve with memory: Content off the multiples, from whatever the state does between one sample and the next.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The stimulus, and not the chain. The chain is far enough down to be irrelevant to either reading: these takes stand fifty-seven to sixty-three decibels over the same chain with nothing played. What bounds both readings is that the products of the voice's own partials sit in the same bins as the stage's own orders, so no floor read in any take separates them and no quieter floor would.
separated_by.why_not_separable: Not by this rig on this unit, and the three ways out are each closed by a measurement rather than by an estimate. A stimulus with no harmonics of its own cannot be presented from outside: this unit's analogue input reaches its output and bypasses every one of its effects, which is a published record here. It cannot be found among the unit's own voices either -- quietening the voice's own orders buys about one more usable order per twenty decibels, so reading as far as the ninth would want a voice whose loudest own order is about a hundred decibels under its first, and the third order alone gives the identity no term it can use. And the curve cannot be driven out from under the contamination, though that would work: its own order k grows as the k-th power of the drive while the products of the stimulus grow as the first, but the input ladder already reaches the part's full volume and the drive byte moves the stage's whole order content from 2.93 decibels under the first at the setting the page rests it at to 4.01 at the top of the byte.

alternatives.reading: What the curve does near zero is a staircase -- a quantiser with a fixed step -- rather than a smooth feature such as a dead zone or a crossover notch. The reading that put a feature near zero in the first place has been withdrawn, so this is not offered as the better of two explanations of something measured. It is asked because the run that would settle it is the same run that would say whether there is a feature near zero at all, and the high orders answer both.

separated_by.observable: How the order series behaves from the eleventh order up, which is where what the stage makes of the voice's own other partials is bounded and below what the takes already show there. Not below it: the ninth order is under that bound and the tenth clears it by a few decibels.

predicts.a staircase: A series that stops falling. A quantiser's error is broadband, so the high orders sit on a plateau instead of continuing down.
predicts.a smooth feature: A series that goes on falling at about the rate the low orders set, because the feature is smooth on the scale of the signal.

separated_by.divergence: 14 dB. Read to thirty-two orders these takes already show a plateau: orders 9 to 17 fall about 1.7 dB an order, which carried to order 30 would put it near -56 dB under the first, and what is there is -42. That figure is not usable as it stands -- the take routed past the effect plateaus in the same place, so on this carrier the plateau is the voice's -- but it is the size the difference would be.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: products of the voice's other partials, which no take here separates from the stage's own orders. They are not in the take routed past the effect, because nothing made them there; they are not halfway to the next order, because they sit on the order. The bound is worked out rather than read: a curve is fed the voice as these takes measure it and driven until it carries the same total order content the unit carries at this rung, -11.24 decibels under the first, which is what sets how much second and third order it has and so how large the products are. The voice's partials' phases are not measured, so the bound is the worst of 12 draws of them. Against that, the ninth order sits 5.2 decibels *under* the bound and cannot be read at all. The tenth clears it by 4.6 decibels and the eleventh by 6.4, and from the eleventh order up the margin is 5.2 to 34.0 decibels. This replaces the bound the alternative was queued with. The voice's own orders being at the chain's floor from the fourteenth upward is true and is not the bound: what the stage makes of the voice's other partials is tens of decibels above the voice's own orders and lands on the same ones. That bound was computed by matching one number, the stand-in's total order content, and the run this alternative asked for showed the match is not one-to-one: the stand-in carries a ripple term and past a drive of about one it folds every low order back, so a target of -9.12 decibels is met at a drive of 0.84 and again at 1.90, whose thirty-first orders are -157 and -79 decibels -- 78 apart for the same matched number. The bound is now anchored on the third, fifth, seventh and ninth orders together, which the ripple cannot fold onto each other at once, and how far the stand-in ended from the unit is reported with every bound it produces. The figure above stands: its own target is met at one drive only, so the branch this repairs never arose for it.

run.stimulus: a note held through the effect on a voice measured to be one component at this same note -- program 79, from a survey of nine of the unit's own voices. Read through the filter these figures are read through, its own orders stand 41.7 decibels under its first at the worst of the first eight, and from the fourteenth order upward it stands at the chain's own floor, 101 decibels under and lower. Not a signal presented at the analogue input: that input reaches this unit's output flat and bypasses every one of its effects, which is measured. The series is read from the eleventh order up and not below it, because what this same stage makes of the voice's other partials lands on the orders themselves and stands over the ninth

alternatives.taken_up_by: The run was made and the claim above now says what it found. The series stops falling: from the 25th order to the 31st it sits 31 decibels over where the rate the low orders set would have put it, which is the staircase's prediction and the opposite of the smooth feature's. Not `ruled_out_by`: this is the reading that turned out to be right. What the run does not carry is the byte -- it reads at one setting, for the reason in `sensitivity_here`.

refuted_by: A drive setting between 8 and 48 whose orders no input level reproduces, by more than the bar the ladder measures at that input. Or the wanted input ceasing to follow the byte's value in decibels once the ladder is extended -- the run reached thirty-six decibels of input and the law was checked over forty of drive, and a longer ladder could break it where this one could not look. Or the output level byte turning out to move the orders after all on some other type, which would make every comparison here a comparison through a gain and the whole reading an artefact of loudness.
what_this_does_not_settle: What the curve is. Nothing here fits one: no polynomial order, no clipping law, no table length, and no statement about whether it is odd, even or neither. This is a stronger disclaimer than the one it replaces, which said the figures say a great deal about the shape and were merely not fitted. They do not. The signal they were read on is two oscillators twelve cents apart at nearly the same size, so what a whole multiple of the carrier holds is not the order of a curve fed a tone -- it is what the stronger of the two made by itself under a drive level that beats through its whole range six times inside every take. A shape cannot be taken off that, and this claim's business is a correspondence between settings, which can.

What the byte does at its bottom three settings. They are one state and the claim says so; it does not say whether the byte is clamped there, whether the gain has a floor under it, or whether something else entirely takes over.
What the byte does above 48. Every setting above it asks for more input than the part can produce, so the ladder cannot reach them and nothing here says whether the law continues, bends or stops.

Whether the other standalone drive type is a gain into its own fixed curve. It is measured to be a different curve; it was never given a ladder of its own, and the same comparison on it is a run that has not been made.

Whether the cabinet after the stage leaves the reading alone. The sweep under a cabinet is published beside this and is not used here, because a filter after a nonlinearity changes which orders come back and the matching would be against a ladder made without one.

How the byte behaves on the fourteen other types that print a drive parameter. Two were asked and they are the two standalone ones; a multi-effect's drive stage is a block-reuse question this says nothing about.

Whether the correspondence is a gain at all rather than a gain and a matched attenuation after it. The reading is a ratio, so anything after the curve is invisible to it by construction -- which is what makes settings of different loudness comparable and is also what it cannot see.

Anything above about the thirteenth order. Read to thirty-two orders the takes still hold energy at the top, but the take routed past the effect holds it too: the carrier's own orders come within 3 dB of what the stage returns by order 15 at the drive the ladder was made at and by order 13 at the top of the byte. What the high orders do is the question that separates the shapes near zero from each other, and this carrier cannot be asked it. Another of the unit's own voices can: a survey of nine of them at this same note found one whose own orders are at the chain's floor from the fourteenth upward. What the stimulus could not provide was the run's choice of stimulus and not a property of the machine.

a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.what: This file was published saying what the curve does, and it had no business saying it. The sentence is recorded rather than deleted, because what is wrong with it is a mistake this archive can make again and the figures it was drawn from have not moved.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.said: That the curve is not a saturating clipper: that its harmonic content falls as the input rises, monotonically over thirty-six decibels, and never reaches the carrier's own orders however quiet the input gets -- so what departs from linearity sits near zero rather than at the extremes. The name carried it too, as `the curve's departure from linearity near zero rather than at its extremes`.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.refuted_by: The take the record itself holds. The voice was picked for being near a single partial, on a figure -- ninety-two per cent of its energy in its own fundamental -- measured at a different note, and the property was not asked again at the note the run moved to. Asked now, off the record's own bypassed take, it is two oscillators eleven to twelve cents apart with the weaker one two to four decibels under the stronger, at every order from the first. A shape read off the response to that is a shape read off two beating tones, and the drive level was moving through sixteen decibels inside every take while it was read.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.what_survived_and_why: The correspondence between settings, which is the claim. It holds for any signal at all: if the stage is one fixed curve behind one gain, scaling what is fed in has the same effect whatever is fed in, so a comparison whose two sides were made on the same signal does not care what the signal was. Every comparison here was. The separation from the other drive type survives for the same reason, and so does the finding that the byte's bottom three settings are one state. What does not survive is every sentence about the curve itself, because those read the figures as a harmonic series and they are not one.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.how_it_was_found: By checking the precondition of the run this file was asking for next. Three of its standing alternatives wanted a synthesised sine put in at the analogue input, and whether that reaches the effects is a published record of this unit -- it does not. Going back for a stimulus the unit could actually provide is what made the present one get looked at.

a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.what: This file published two readings of the stage's phases against the alternative that the curve has a state in it. Neither was a reading. They are recorded rather than deleted, because what is wrong with them is a mistake this archive can make again -- it is the second time a sentence about this stage has been read off a stimulus nobody asked the right question of -- and because the figures themselves have not moved.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.said: That between the whole multiples the routed take stands over the voice by 10.8 decibels at the lowest of three carriers against 3.2 and 1.8 at the two above it; and that at that same lowest carrier seven of eight orders' angles moved with the drive by twenty-six to a hundred and nine degrees while the two upper carriers moved none. Both were offered as readings that single out one carrier, and neither was written as the answer.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.refuted_by: Both readings rest on one sentence, and the sentence has a condition in it that was never checked: a curve with no state in it, fed one steady tone, returns every order along the carrier or exactly against it. The stimulus is not one steady tone. It is one of this unit's own voices, and these records' own control takes publish its orders at 41.7 to 51.4 decibels under its first. Read off the same takes, it carries a second series at half multiples that no survey asked for, at 61.9 to 82.8 decibels under its first -- the same series at all three notes, agreeing partial for partial to within 1.6 of a decibel across three entirely different sets of frequencies, which is a sampled voice transposed by playback rate. Rendered against that stimulus, a curve with no state in it breaks the drive sweep by 69 degrees on 10 orders and the two-carrier identity by 89; a curve with a state inside it breaks them by 92 and 59. Both readings break on both curves, and which of the two breaks further is not even the same for the two readings. A reading that comes out the same way whichever the stage is separates nothing. What does it is arithmetic and not a floor: products of the stimulus's own components land on the same integer grid the curve's own orders land on, at the same frequencies, in the same bins. Fed the whole voice against the fundamental alone at the same level, a memoryless curve puts order three within 3 degrees and +0.0 of a decibel of where the fundamental alone puts it, order five 35 degrees and +3.7 decibels away, and order nine 73 degrees and +26.2 decibels away. Only the third order is the curve's. The between-the-multiples half has a second thing wrong with it besides: it is read at the exact half multiple, and the half multiple is where this voice has a line. That reading was measuring the voice's own partial and what a memoryless curve makes of it.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.what_survived_and_why: Every size reading in the file, and that is all of the claim. None of them needed one steady tone: the input ladder, the gain the stage gives the carrier, where the output comes to rest, the tilt between three carriers and the fixed filter it puts in front of the curve, and the correspondence between settings the claim is. A comparison whose two sides were made on the same signal does not care what the signal was, and every one of those was.
a_reading_published_and_withdrawn.how_it_was_found: By pricing the run this file had booked against the alternative before booking the unit for it. The run was to bound what the chain itself makes of a signal at the level the routed take arrives at, on the argument that the take routed past the effect is twelve to twenty-three decibels too quiet to bound it. That argument compares the two ladders rung for rung. Compared across the rungs -- a routed take at one rung against a bypassed take at a louder one is the same chain at the same level -- the bypassed ladder already passes within 3.2 decibels of every level the routed ladder reaches, against the twenty-three the run was booked on. The booked run would have found the chain innocent and left the reading standing. Asking what the reading was standing on instead is what found this. The argument was already written down one step short: this alternative's own `sensitivity_here` says that a curve fed two tones returns products between them and that those land off the multiples whether or not anything has memory. It was asked of the voice that was replaced and not of the voice that replaced it.
